newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate, baht down in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate, baht down in late trade.

text.p: Rising liquidity pushed the Thai overnight interbank rate down further to 12.00 percent late on Monday from 12.50 in the morning and 13.00 late on Friday, dealers said.
Dealers said liquidity improved on moderate dollar selling and inflows of foreign funds triggered by Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa's decision to dissolve parliament and call fresh elections.
"The market saw some dollar offering today after news of parliament dissolution and fresh elections," said a currency dealer at a local bank.
Banharn set November 17 as general election day.
The baht eased to 25.417-25.240 to the dollar near the close from 25.406-25.411 in the morning on a firmer dollar in major foreign markets, dealers said.
Dollar's gain against the baht was restrained by selling of the U.S. unit and baht's improved sentiment, dealers said.

"Some dollar offers kept the dollar/baht rate below midrate throughout the day despite the dollar's sharp rise against the majors," said the dealer. "For the time being, yes, sentiment for the baht is improving."
Dealers said foreign confidence in the Thai financial market is rising on expectations that Thailand will have a more qualified economic team to tackle economic problems after the general elections.
One-month baht/dollar swap premium was quoted at 10.00/10.50 satangs per dollar late against 10.00/10.75 in the morning.
The baht/dollar mid-rate was fixed by the central bank at 25.42 against 25.41 on Friday.
